# ALGORITHM: Atomic scoring
#   source:      journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §V
#   complexity:  O(n) time · O(1) space (n = number of items in session)
#   parameters:  score = COUNT(correct) / COUNT(total) * 100, rounded to 2 decimal places
#   security:    Scoring happens server-side in Postgres function — never on client
#   invariants:
#     - submit_exam_session sets completed_at on the session (closes the time window)
#     - Attempt record is created atomically with scoring in same transaction
#     - Score is computed from session_answers joined to correct options — not client-provided
#     - Once completed_at is set, time-windowed RLS blocks further item access
#     - Double-submit is prevented by checking completed_at IS NULL
#
# DATA STRUCTURE: Postgres transaction (atomic submission)
#   source:  journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §VI
#   ops:     Single RPC: UPDATE session + INSERT attempt + compute score — all atomic
#   where:   packages/db/rpc/submit-exam-session.sql

## Summary
Build the submit_exam_session Postgres RPC that atomically finalizes an exam session, computes the score from saved answers, and creates an attempt record in a single transaction.

## User story
As a student, I want to submit my exam and see my score, knowing that all my auto-saved answers are scored atomically and no data can be lost between "submit" and "scored."

## Why this matters
If submission is not atomic, a crash between marking the session complete and creating the attempt record leaves a completed session with no grade. The student sees "submitted" but has no score. Faculty sees no attempt. The time-windowed RLS (C02) depends on completed_at being set to close the window. Atomic scoring in a single RPC prevents all these failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] submit_exam_session RPC sets completed_at on exam_sessions
- [ ] RPC computes score: COUNT(correct answers) / COUNT(total items) * 100
- [ ] RPC creates an exam_attempts record with session_id, student_id, score, submitted_at
- [ ] All three operations happen in a single Postgres transaction (atomic)
- [ ] Double-submit is prevented (completed_at IS NOT NULL returns error)
- [ ] Expired sessions are auto-submitted with whatever answers were saved
- [ ] After submission, time-windowed RLS blocks further item access (verified)
- [ ] Inngest event journey/session.completed fires after successful submission
- [ ] API route POST /api/exams/[id]/submit returns the score and attempt_id

## Canonical decisions in play
| Rule | What it means for this story |
|---|---|
| C01 | Atomic submission — score computed from auto-saved answers, never lost |
| C02 | completed_at closes the time window — RLS enforces post-submit lockout |
| AP-17 | Sequential inserts BANNED — must use supabase.rpc('submit_exam_session') |
| Rule 6 (G08) | Supabase-first — attempts live in Supabase, no Neo4j write |
| Data Layer | createServerClient() in API route, Row<'exam_attempts'> for types |

## Schema changes
```sql
-- exam_attempts table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.exam_attempts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  session_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.exam_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  student_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.profiles(id),
  exam_id UUID NOT NULL,
  institution_id UUID NOT NULL,
  score NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL, -- 0.00 to 100.00
  total_items INTEGER NOT NULL,
  correct_items INTEGER NOT NULL,
  submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (session_id)
);

-- RLS on attempts
ALTER TABLE public.exam_attempts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Students can read own attempts"
  ON public.exam_attempts FOR SELECT
  USING (student_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Faculty can read institution attempts"
  ON public.exam_attempts FOR SELECT
  USING (
    institution_id = (
      SELECT institution_id FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()
    )
    AND (SELECT role FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()) IN ('admin', 'faculty')
  );

-- submit_exam_session RPC
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.submit_exam_session(
  p_session_id UUID,
  p_student_id UUID
)
RETURNS JSON
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_exam_id UUID;
  v_institution_id UUID;
  v_total INTEGER;
  v_correct INTEGER;
  v_score NUMERIC(5,2);
  v_attempt_id UUID;
  v_submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ := now();
BEGIN
  -- Verify session exists, belongs to student, and is not already completed
  SELECT exam_id, institution_id INTO v_exam_id, v_institution_id
  FROM public.exam_sessions
  WHERE id = p_session_id
    AND student_id = p_student_id
    AND completed_at IS NULL;

  IF v_exam_id IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Session not found, not owned by student, or already submitted';
  END IF;

  -- Count total items
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_total
  FROM public.session_items
  WHERE session_id = p_session_id;

  -- Count correct answers
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_correct
  FROM public.session_answers sa
  JOIN public.session_items si ON si.id = sa.session_item_id
  JOIN public.assessment_item_options aio ON aio.id = sa.selected_option_id
  WHERE sa.session_id = p_session_id
    AND aio.is_correct = true;

  -- Compute score
  v_score := CASE
    WHEN v_total = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE ROUND((v_correct::NUMERIC / v_total::NUMERIC) * 100, 2)
  END;

  -- Mark session complete (closes time-windowed RLS)
  UPDATE public.exam_sessions
  SET completed_at = v_submitted_at
  WHERE id = p_session_id;

  -- Create attempt record
  INSERT INTO public.exam_attempts (
    session_id, student_id, exam_id, institution_id,
    score, total_items, correct_items, submitted_at
  )
  VALUES (
    p_session_id, p_student_id, v_exam_id, v_institution_id,
    v_score, v_total, v_correct, v_submitted_at
  )
  RETURNING id INTO v_attempt_id;

  RETURN json_build_object(
    'attempt_id', v_attempt_id,
    'score', v_score,
    'total_items', v_total,
    'correct_items', v_correct,
    'submitted_at', v_submitted_at
  );
END;
$$;
```

## API contract
```
POST /app/api/exams/[id]/submit
Headers: Cookie (student session)
Request: { session_id: string }
Response 200: { data: { attempt_id, score, total_items, correct_items, submitted_at }, error: null }
Response 400: { data: null, error: { code: 'ALREADY_SUBMITTED', message: 'Session already submitted' } }
Response 400: { data: null, error: { code: 'SESSION_NOT_FOUND', message: 'Session not found or not owned' } }
Response 401: { data: null, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Not authenticated' } }
```

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// features/exam-delivery/services/ExamSubmitService.ts
import { createServerClient } from '@journey/db/client';
import type { Row } from '@journey/db/client';
import { inngest } from '@journey/inngest/client';

type ExamAttempt = Row<'exam_attempts'>;

export class ExamSubmitService {
  async submitExam(sessionId: string, studentId: string) {
    const supabase = createServerClient();

    // Atomic RPC — AP-17 compliant
    const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('submit_exam_session', {
      p_session_id: sessionId,
      p_student_id: studentId,
    });

    if (error) {
      if (error.message.includes('already submitted')) {
        throw new Error('ALREADY_SUBMITTED');
      }
      throw error;
    }

    // Emit Inngest event after successful submission
    await inngest.send({
      name: 'journey/session.completed',
      data: {
        attempt_id: data.attempt_id,
        session_id: sessionId,
        student_id: studentId,
        score: data.score,
        submitted_at: data.submitted_at,
      },
    });

    return data;
  }
}

// app/api/exams/[id]/submit/route.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { createServerClient } from '@journey/db/client';
import { ExamSubmitService } from '@/features/exam-delivery/services/ExamSubmitService';

export async function POST(
  req: NextRequest,
  { params }: { params: { id: string } }
) {
  const supabase = createServerClient();
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();

  if (!user) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { data: null, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Not authenticated' } },
      { status: 401 }
    );
  }

  const { session_id } = await req.json();
  const service = new ExamSubmitService();

  try {
    const result = await service.submitExam(session_id, user.id);
    return NextResponse.json({ data: result, error: null });
  } catch (err) {
    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Unknown error';
    const code = message === 'ALREADY_SUBMITTED' ? 'ALREADY_SUBMITTED' : 'SUBMISSION_FAILED';
    return NextResponse.json(
      { data: null, error: { code, message } },
      { status: 400 }
    );
  }
}
```

## Code patterns to AVOID
```typescript
// ✗ AP-17: Sequential operations for atomic submission — BANNED
await supabase.from('exam_sessions').update({ completed_at: now });
// If crash happens HERE, session is "completed" but no attempt exists!
const score = computeScoreOnClient(answers); // BANNED — client-computed score
await supabase.from('exam_attempts').insert({ score }); // BANNED — sequential

// ✓ Use: supabase.rpc('submit_exam_session', {...}) — single atomic transaction

// ✗ Client-provided score
const { score } = await req.json(); // BANNED — score computed server-side in RPC

// ✗ Missing double-submit guard
// Not checking completed_at IS NULL — student can submit twice and get two attempts
```

## Automated tests (Playwright — runs during /validate)
```typescript
// tests/E07/E07-S08.api.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('POST /api/exams/[id]/submit creates attempt with score', async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/exams/test-exam-id/submit', {
    data: { session_id: 'test-session-id' }
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
  const { data } = await res.json();
  expect(data.attempt_id).toBeTruthy();
  expect(data.score).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  expect(data.score).toBeLessThanOrEqual(100);
  expect(data.total_items).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(data.submitted_at).toBeTruthy();
});

test('Double submit returns 400 ALREADY_SUBMITTED', async ({ request }) => {
  // First submit
  await request.post('/api/exams/test-exam-id/submit', {
    data: { session_id: 'test-session-id' }
  });
  // Second submit
  const res = await request.post('/api/exams/test-exam-id/submit', {
    data: { session_id: 'test-session-id' }
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(400);
  const body = await res.json();
  expect(body.error.code).toBe('ALREADY_SUBMITTED');
});

test('After submit, student cannot read assessment items (RLS window closed)', async ({ request }) => {
  // Submit the session
  await request.post('/api/exams/test-exam-id/submit', {
    data: { session_id: 'test-session-id' }
  });
  // Try to read items
  const res = await request.get('/api/assessment-items');
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
  const { data } = await res.json();
  expect(data.items).toHaveLength(0); // RLS blocks post-submit access
});

test('Negative: unauthenticated request returns 401', async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.post('/api/exams/test-exam-id/submit', {
    data: { session_id: 'test-session-id' }
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(401);
});
```

## Rollback procedure
If implementation fails mid-way:
1. `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.submit_exam_session;`
2. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.exam_attempts CASCADE;`
3. No Neo4j changes to revert.
4. `git stash && git checkout develop`
